beats.say: This is how to use demo-presentation, from install to a reviewed video, in seven steps.
Your machine needs only uv and git. Python, Chromium, ffmpeg and the voice install on first use.
Step one: install the skill. In Claude Code, it's a plugin, and this repo is its own marketplace.

do.comment: Claude Code plugin (or /plugin install … at its prompt)

beats.say: Any other agent that reads SKILL.md files can add it with npx skills.
Or download the zip from the releases page, and unzip it into your agent's skills folder.

do.comment: or by hand: unzip the release into your skills folder

beats.say: Whichever way you choose, you end up with this folder: the skill file, the command line in scripts, and the scene renderers.
Step two: give your project a .demo folder. Its config.toml sets the theme and the voice.
The lexicon fixes words the voice would get wrong, like ffmpeg and uv.
A web app also sets a base URL, and the services to start before recording. Here, that's a small sample app.
brief.md tells the agent what it may show: routes, selectors, safe commands, and what never goes on camera. The agent reads it before it plans a single scene.
Then make sure git ignores the runs and local folders. Videos never belong in the repo.
Step three: ask your agent for a video, in plain words.

do.type: make a demo video of the new settings page

beats.say: Name the feature, the PR, or the idea. Say outline first if you want to approve a plan before it records.

do.type: record a walkthrough of this PR, outline first

beats.say: Step four is the agent's job. It creates a run with demo new, and writes the script.
Then demo storyboard renders one frame per beat in seconds, and the agent checks every frame itself.
Only then does demo build narrate, record in real time, and stitch the final video.
Here's a finished run. It holds the script, the storyboard, the scene clips and the final video.
And validate checks a script before anything is rendered.
Remember the settings page you asked for? This is the kind of UI scene the agent records, here on the sample app.

chapter.title: Your app
chapter.description: a UI scene on the sample app

beats.say: It drives a real browser, and clicks through to the settings page like a person would.
A spotlight points at whatever the narration is talking about.
It turns on the weekly digest, and waits until the app says it saved.
And it types into the page, just as you would.
UI scenes aren't limited to your machine. A scene can open any site, like this project's page on GitHub.
For a site behind a login, the token comes from an environment variable, never from the script.
Step five: review it in the browser. The agent gives you a link from demo url, a page on your own machine.
It opens on the video, with a live transcript underneath. Press space to play.
Click any word in the transcript to jump to it, and use the arrow keys to step through.
To comment, pause where something should change and press C. The comment is pinned to that moment.
Write what you want changed.
Press Mark region, and drag over the part of the frame you mean.
Then add it. It joins the list on the right, and a pin marks it on the timeline.
If the voice says a word wrong, pause and click that word.
Press Edit pronunciation, write how it should sound, and press Listen to check it.
Save puts it in the project's pronunciation library, so every video says it that way.
The Script and storyboard tab shows every beat with its frame. You can edit the narration right here.
Or press Request change on a scene or a beat, and say what you want.

fill.text: Say the file name out loud.

beats.say: Change requests collects them all in one place for the agent.
Re-render changes runs the same commands the agent would, for only what changed.
When it's right, press Approve video. If not, tell your agent you left feedback, or paste it the prompt from Copy agent prompt.
The agent reads your comments with demo review. Each one is mapped to its beat.
It edits the script, re-renders only the scenes that changed, replies to every comment, and sends you the link again.

beats.say: Step six is optional. If your team keeps videos somewhere else, add a publish command to config.toml.
demo publish runs it with the video, captions and title in environment variables, and the agent passes on whatever it prints.
Step seven, when something goes wrong: start with demo doctor. It shows what's installed and what will install on first use.

beats.say: If screenshots fail with unable to capture, add the software GL flag to storyboard and build.

do.comment: "Unable to capture screenshot": render without the GPU

beats.say: And if a UI scene times out, storyboard it with the headed flag to watch the browser, and check the selector.

do.comment: a UI scene times out: watch it in a real window

beats.say: That's it: install, set up .demo, ask, let the agent build, review, and publish if you want to.

items: install: plugin, npx skills, or the zip
ask → the agent storyboards and builds
publish if you want; demo doctor if stuck
